exposure: Cervical septum incision (during hysteroscopic transcervical incision of the uterine septum)
Preservation of cervical septum (during hysteroscopic transcervical incision of the uterine septum)
cohort: The study included 105 women with complete septate uterus and duplicated cervix who underwent hysteroscopic transcervical incision of the uterine septum at a hospital in Shanghai, China, between January 2008 and December 2020.
finding: Preserving the cervical septum during hysteroscopic transcervical incision of the uterine septum resulted in significantly improved reproductive outcomes, including lower abortion rates, lower preterm birth rates, higher full-term birth rates, and reduced incidence of premature rupture of membranes and cervical incompetence.
